scenes.tts: Your gut lining is a sheet just one cell thick. How does it keep pulling glucose into your blood, even when the gut holds less than the blood?
scenes.narration: Your gut lining is a sheet just one cell thick. How does it keep pulling glucose into your blood, even when the gut holds less than the blood?
scenes.caption: Your gut lining is a sheet just one cell thick. How does it keep pulling glucose into your blood, even when the gut holds less than the blood?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: glucose GOLD dots; sodium BLUE dots; the sodium pump and ATP RED; the seal between cells GREEN; apical face a bright WHITE line; basolateral face (sides and base) a darker SLATE line; cells pale grey fill. Layout: three tall gut-lining cells side by side across the middle of the frame, filling about 65% of frame height, the middle cell slightly brighter. Above them a band labelled 'gut' (the lumen); below them a dark band labelled 'blood' with a slow left-to-right flow of faint dots. Right edge: two vertical level gauges filled GOLD, labelled 'gut glucose' and 'blood glucose', with a small 'schematic' tag under them. The blood gauge stays fixed all film. Motion during the line: gold glucose dots drift down out of the gut band, enter the cells at the top and leave at the bottom into the blood band, where they are carried off by the flow. The gut gauge falls steadily as the gut band empties of gold; on 'even when the gut holds less', the gut gauge sinks to the level of the blood gauge and a dashed line marks that level across both gauges. On the question, white text appears across the top: 'Uphill?'
Title 'Two Faces and a Seal' fades in over the top band for 2 s while gold dots keep drifting through the cells; the 'Uphill?' text fades out beneath it. Gauges rewind smoothly to a full gut.

scenes.tts: Its top, the apical face, looks into the gut. Its sides and base, the basolateral face, look toward its neighbours and the blood. Each face carries different proteins.
scenes.narration: Its top, the apical face, looks into the gut. Its sides and base, the basolateral face, look toward its neighbours and the blood. Each face carries different proteins.
scenes.caption: Its top, the apical face, looks into the gut. Its sides and base, the basolateral face, look toward its neighbours and the blood. Each face carries different proteins.
scenes.visual: On the first words, a slow push-in until the middle cell fills about 70% of frame height; its neighbours stay visible at the edges and the gauges stay at the right. On 'apical face' the top membrane brightens to a thick WHITE line and gets the label 'apical' (size 30). On 'basolateral face' the two sides and the base brighten to SLATE and get the label 'basolateral'. On 'different proteins' small empty slots appear: one on the white top, two on the slate base, each pulsing gently, waiting to be filled.

scenes.tts: On the apical face sits a carrier called S G L T one, a sodium glucose carrier. Think of it as a turnstile. Two sodium ions and one glucose pass through it together.
scenes.narration: On the apical face sits a carrier called SGLT1, a sodium-glucose carrier. Think of it as a turnstile. Two sodium ions and one glucose pass through it together.
scenes.caption: On the apical face sits a carrier called SGLT1, a sodium-glucose carrier. Think of it as a turnstile. Two sodium ions and one glucose pass through it together.
scenes.visual: The slot on the white top grows into a revolving-door cartoon labelled 'SGLT1 (turnstile)'. Blue sodium dots crowd the gut band. The turnstile turns one notch: exactly two BLUE dots and one GOLD dot pass through together into the cell. It repeats every 2 s for the rest of the film whenever the cell is on screen.

scenes.tts: Sodium is crowded outside the cell and sparse inside, and the inside is negative. So sodium falls inward, downhill. That fall, not the turnstile itself, pays the fare for glucose to climb.
scenes.narration: Sodium is crowded outside the cell and sparse inside, and the inside is negative. So sodium falls inward, downhill. That fall, not the turnstile itself, pays the fare for glucose to climb.
scenes.caption: Sodium is crowded outside the cell and sparse inside, and the inside is negative. So sodium falls inward, downhill. That fall, not the turnstile itself, pays the fare for glucose to climb.
scenes.visual: Behind the cell, a BLUE slope appears: high on the gut side (many blue dots), low inside the cell (few blue dots), with a small minus sign glowing inside the cell. Label 'sodium: downhill' along the slope. At the turnstile, each pair of blue dots slides down the slope as the gold dot is lifted up a short GOLD step labelled 'glucose: uphill'. A coin icon passes from the blue dots to the turnstile on 'pays the fare'.

scenes.tts: Inside, glucose piles up a little. It leaves through a free exit door on the basolateral face. That door is a passive carrier: it spends no energy, and glucose runs out downhill. It is GLUT two in the standard account.
scenes.narration: Inside, glucose piles up a little. It leaves through a free exit door on the basolateral face. That door is a passive carrier: it spends no energy, and glucose runs out downhill. It is GLUT2 in the standard account.
scenes.caption: Inside, glucose piles up a little. It leaves through a free exit door on the basolateral face. That door is a passive carrier: it spends no energy, and glucose runs out downhill. It is GLUT2 in the standard account.
scenes.visual: Gold dots gather loosely inside the cell. A slot on the slate base opens into a plain swinging door labelled 'GLUT2 (exit door)'. Gold dots leave through it one at a time into the blood band and are carried off by the flow. No sodium goes through the door.

scenes.tts: Each glucose brought two sodium ions in. The sodium pump, also on the basolateral face, spends A T P to throw sodium back out. That keeps the slope steep.
scenes.narration: Each glucose brought two sodium ions in. The sodium pump, also on the basolateral face, spends ATP to throw sodium back out. That keeps the slope steep.
scenes.caption: Each glucose brought two sodium ions in. The sodium pump, also on the basolateral face, spends ATP to throw sodium back out. That keeps the slope steep.
scenes.visual: Blue dots that came through the turnstile start to collect inside the cell and the blue slope visibly flattens a little. The second slot on the base becomes a RED pump cartoon labelled 'sodium pump'. A RED 'ATP' token clicks into it and the pump ejects blue dots out of the base into the blood side; the blue dots inside thin out and the slope steepens back to its starting height.

scenes.tts: Now run the clock. The gut's glucose gauge falls to the blood's level, then keeps falling below it. Glucose is moving uphill.
scenes.narration: Now run the clock. The gut's glucose gauge falls to the blood's level, then keeps falling below it. Glucose is moving uphill.
scenes.caption: Now run the clock. The gut's glucose gauge falls to the blood's level, then keeps falling below it. Glucose is moving uphill.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the three-cell world. A clock icon spins at top left. All three cells run the turnstile, door and pump together. The gut band empties of gold; the gut gauge falls past the dashed blood line and keeps going down. On 'uphill', a GOLD arrow appears beside the gauges pointing from the low gut gauge up to the higher blood gauge, labelled 'uphill'.
No narration; motion continues. The gut gauge keeps sinking slowly toward the bottom of its scale; turnstiles keep turning, gold dots keep leaving into the flowing blood band. Nothing is frozen.

scenes.tts: What sets the direction? Under these gut gradients, the carriers' places do. A sodium-paid turnstile on top and a free exit door underneath bias glucose from gut to blood.
scenes.narration: What sets the direction? Under these gut gradients, the carriers' places do. A sodium-paid turnstile on top and a free exit door underneath bias glucose from gut to blood.
scenes.caption: What sets the direction? Under these gut gradients, the carriers' places do. A sodium-paid turnstile on top and a free exit door underneath bias glucose from gut to blood.
scenes.visual: Freeze the dots softly (they keep a gentle bob). The middle cell is outlined; its WHITE top with the turnstile and SLATE base with the exit door and pump pulse in turn. A large arrow fills the cell from top to bottom: 'gut to blood'. Text at the top: 'Where carriers sit sets the direction.'

scenes.tts: Now look between the cells. Neighbours are joined near the top by a seal. Try a thought experiment: loosen that seal enough to let glucose slip through. Would the gut still take up glucose?
scenes.narration: Now look between the cells. Neighbours are joined near the top by a seal. Try a thought experiment: loosen that seal enough to let glucose slip through. Would the gut still take up glucose?
scenes.caption: Now look between the cells. Neighbours are joined near the top by a seal. Try a thought experiment: loosen that seal enough to let glucose slip through. Would the gut still take up glucose?
scenes.visual: Camera slides to the gap between the middle cell and its right neighbour. A GREEN band joins them near the top, labelled 'seal'. On 'thought experiment', a small white tag 'thought experiment' appears beside the seal and stays through s14. On 'loosen', the green band flickers and thins, opening a narrow gap. Rewind the gauges to a full gut (gut gauge well above the dashed blood line). Question card at the top in white: 'Open the seal: does the gut still take up glucose?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the gauges hold, the green seal shimmers faintly at its gap, gold dots bob in place.

scenes.tts: It depends on the gut. Between the cells, glucose just follows its own gradient. Early in a meal, the gut holds more than the blood, so the open seal adds to absorption.
scenes.narration: It depends on the gut. Between the cells, glucose just follows its own gradient. Early in a meal, the gut holds more than the blood, so the open seal adds to absorption.
scenes.caption: It depends on the gut. Between the cells, glucose just follows its own gradient. Early in a meal, the gut holds more than the blood, so the open seal adds to absorption.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. Clock restarts. Gold dots now stream through the turnstiles AND down through the open green gap into the blood. A second small gold arrow labelled 'leak' points down through the gap. The gut gauge falls faster than before (ghost of the earlier fall shown as a faint dashed track for comparison).

scenes.tts: Late in the meal, the gut holds less than the blood. Now the leak runs backwards. Glucose slides back out between the cells, and the gut level stalls at a floor it cannot sink below.
scenes.narration: Late in the meal, the gut holds less than the blood. Now the leak runs backwards. Glucose slides back out between the cells, and the gut level stalls at a floor it cannot sink below.
scenes.caption: Late in the meal, the gut holds less than the blood. Now the leak runs backwards. Glucose slides back out between the cells, and the gut level stalls at a floor it cannot sink below.
scenes.visual: The gut gauge reaches the dashed blood line and dips below it. The 'leak' arrow in the gap turns around and points UP: gold dots drift from the blood band back up through the gap into the gut, while the turnstiles keep carrying gold in. The gut gauge slows and stops at a level below the blood line but well above the bottom of its scale; a short GOLD tick marks it, labelled 'floor'.

scenes.tts: Tighten the seal, and the floor drops. In this thought experiment, what the sheet absorbs is what it carries through the cells, minus what leaks back between them.
scenes.narration: Tighten the seal, and the floor drops. In this thought experiment, what the sheet absorbs is what it carries through the cells, minus what leaks back between them.
scenes.caption: Tighten the seal, and the floor drops. In this thought experiment, what the sheet absorbs is what it carries through the cells, minus what leaks back between them.
scenes.visual: The green seal closes to a solid band; the backward stream through the gap stops; the gut gauge resumes falling and the 'floor' tick slides down. Caption appears at the bottom and stays to the end of the scene: 'net = carried through − leaked back'.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Under the usual gut gradients, where the carriers sit biases glucose flow from gut to blood. The seal does not orient that pathway. It decides what can slip between the cells, and so what can leak back.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Under the usual gut gradients, where the carriers sit biases glucose flow from gut to blood. The seal does not orient that pathway. It decides what can slip between the cells, and so what can leak back.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Under the usual gut gradients, where the carriers sit biases glucose flow from gut to blood. The seal does not orient that pathway. It decides what can slip between the cells, and so what can leak back.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full three-cell world with gauges; the 'thought experiment' tag fades out. On 'where the carriers sit' the turnstiles on the white tops and the exit doors and pumps on the slate bases pulse, and the large 'gut to blood' arrow returns. On 'The seal' the green bands pulse; on 'slip between the cells' a few gold and blue dots jiggle in the gaps without crossing, and a small two-headed arrow appears in one gap labelled 'what can pass'.

scenes.tts: Our glucose leak was a thought experiment. What the real seal lets through, and how it is measured, is in the text below.
scenes.narration: Our glucose leak was a thought experiment. What the real seal lets through, and how it is measured, is in the text below.
scenes.caption: Our glucose leak was a thought experiment. What the real seal lets through, and how it is measured, is in the text below.
scenes.visual: Slow pan down the side wall between two cells to the green seal, which zooms slightly; then on past it to a stack of plain grey unlabelled blocks further down the side and at the base (other junctions, schematic). The gauges slide out of frame. Text in white: 'The real seal: in the text below'.
End card over the dimmed world, large white text, centred: 'Usual gut gradients: carrier placement biases glucose flow toward blood.' Gold dots still drift slowly through the cells behind it.
